line: You're 3B? I'm Chen, from 4A. I saw your name on the mailbox. Are you eating properly? Everyone your age eats standing up.
choice2: Nice to meet you, Mrs. Chen.
choice3: Sorry, I really have to go.

line: I knew it. Saturday I'm ordering from Golden Wheat for my grandson's class. Kevin wants thirty egg tarts. I'll get extra for you.
choice2: You don't have to do that.
choice3: Thank you. I should get going.

line: It's nothing. Kevin is nine. Saturdays he's at the school at the center, Chinese in the morning, chess after lunch. He likes the chess better. Don't tell his mother.
choice2: What do you do while he's there?
choice3: I'll let you go, Mrs. Chen.

line: I know I don't have to. Golden Wheat gives thirteen for the price of twelve, so somebody has to eat the thirteenth. Better you than my blood pressure.
With his mother, on Elm. My daughter is on nights at the hospital this month, so Kevin sleeps at my place Tuesdays. He brings his own pillow. Very serious about the pillow.
choice1: Do you spend a lot of time at the center?

line: Seniors' lunch, Tuesdays and Saturdays. I'm on the dish crew. Forty people, two sinks, and Mr. Guo telling everyone where to stand. Have you been yet?
Go once properly. People will ask your family name, where your parents are from, if you're married. Answer the first one. The rest, smile. That's what I do.
choice3: I'll keep it in mind. I should go.

line: Not bad. Everybody just knows everybody. Saturday, noon. Come to the kitchen door, not the front, and I'll put you on bowls instead of in the line. Eat first.
choice2: I'll try. Nice to meet you, Mrs. Chen.

line: My tablet class moved to Wednesdays and nobody told me. I sat there forty minutes with the tai chi group.
choice1: Did you at least do the tai chi?

line: Kevin's school wants a grandparent to talk about Lunar New Year in his class. Will you come with me? My English gets nervous in front of children.
choice3: Let me think about it and get back to you.

line: Good. Thursday after lunch. I'm bringing red envelopes with chocolate coins, not money. Last year a grandfather gave real dollars and the teacher sent a letter home.
choice1: What are you going to talk about?
choice2: Can I help you get ready?
choice3: I should get going, but I'll be there.

line: Nobody is good with nine-year-olds. You stand next to me and nod. If they ask about firecrackers, you answer, because I'll say something the teacher doesn't like.
choice2: Let's talk about it another time.

line: The calendar, the food, why we clean the house before and not after. I wrote it all on cards. My daughter says too many cards. Twelve cards is not too many.
choice2: What do you need for the day?
choice3: I'll let you get back to your cards.

line: You can carry the oranges. Also the poster, Kevin drew it. The rabbit has six legs. We are not fixing it.
choice2: I should get going for now.

line: Card one: 'Lunar New Year is the most important holiday in China.' My daughter says 'for many families,' because Kevin's friends Minh and Ji-woo have it too. Which is right?
choice3: Can we pick this up another time?

line: Then I fix four cards. I think Kevin doesn't want me to come. He says, 'Nai Nai, just don't do the voice.' What voice? This is my voice.
choice2: Do the voice. They'll love it.

line: Hm. You sound like my daughter, but nicer. Okay. Thursday, one o'clock, front office. Wear something red, not too much. And eat lunch sitting down.
choice2: I'll do my best. See you, Mrs. Chen.

line: Kevin's school sent home a form asking where everyone in the house was born. His mother left it on the counter a week. Nobody wants to fill it in.
choice1: You don't have to answer everything on those.

line: The center got a grant for a social worker who speaks Mandarin and Cantonese. Finally I can retire from reading everyone's Medicare letters.

I never see you at the center anymore. Busy with your library friends? I'm teasing. Mostly.
Oh. Hello.
choice1: Mrs. Chen, I'm sorry I rushed off before.

line: Not now, I'm adding up the lunch money in my head. Don't talk, I'll lose the number.

line: Not now, I'm counting lunch bowls. Thirty-two. Thirty-three...
Mrs. Chen, in a tracksuit, has just finished with the tai chi group under the far trees. "Forty minutes. My knees are complaining in two languages."
